body_html:
Four years ago, for a brief period of time, I went to the dark side.
Yes, I’m not proud to admit it, but I actually wrote a jQuery-plugin: jPolygon!
These days I only write Vanilla JS — I write whatever I’m told to write!

Anyway, the old jQuery-plugin has been updated to Vanilla JS. A bunch of new features have been added — and, most important: I’ve added the ability to save and view the output as SVG.

As the plugin/app utilizes a bunch of new(er) HTML5-elements, such as:

<input type="range">
<input type="color">
<input type="number">
<details><summary>Fold-Out Stuff</summary></details>

—I recommend using Google Chrome.

Kudos must go to my good ‘ol friend, Torben, who helped with the math behind the original function for calculating points in a polygon: a beautiful, 10-line function that does all the hard work.

So, go ahead and create some polygons!
If you need “tactical elements”, such as a splash like “Save 10%”, it looks so much better with SVG than, say PNG, on a retina-display.

If you do want a PNG, however, there’s also a big green button, “Generate PNG”, just for that.

Click here to see a live demo!

To view, edit or fumble with the code, go to the Github-page.
